title: Why your agents need decision traces, not just documents — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j
talk_summary: Neo4j pitches 'context graphs': storing past decisions as graph nodes (entities, events, policies) with causal links, then retrieving similar past decision traces via combined semantic + structural (graph) embeddings to inform new decisions. The concrete mechanism is a decision-trace store queried by precedent, plus an open-source scaffolding tool and an agent-memory package (short-term, long-term, reasoning).

takeaways.what_they_do: Record each past decision (approve/reject, review verdict, root cause) as a node linked to the entities and policies it involved, so future agents retrieve 'precedents' rather than just documents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's also going to get you past decision traces and precedents, and dynamic information about why decisions are made

takeaways.technique: Hybrid semantic + structural similarity for precedent lookup
takeaways.what_they_do: Combine a vector index over text with a 'graph embedding' over the connected decision-trace subgraph, so similar traces are found by both wording and causal structure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: both on semantic similarity and structural similarity inside of the graph that actually looked at how the decision traces were made

takeaways.what_they_do: Separate conversation/session context (short-term), deduplicated resolved entities (long-term), and reasoning traces (the decision graph), with an extraction pipeline (spaCy -> gliner -> LLM fallback) plus merge/dedup/enrich stages.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a short-term memory, a long-term memory and reasoning

takeaways.technique: Scaffold + MCP server generation for a domain graph
takeaways.what_they_do: A one-line CLI generates backend, frontend, ontology/schema, seed data, and an MCP server for a chosen domain and agent framework.
takeaways.evidence_quote: generating an MCP server and doing actually multi-turn conversation inside of that app

takeaways.what_they_do: Speaker concedes they have not solved scoring stored decisions, but flags attaching a quality score to each decision trace as the needed next step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's something to think about like some sort of sentiment or um like quality score on the decisions
